lesson_title: Loans, Hire Purchase and Insurance: the True Price of Pay-Later
hook_text: The advert says R3 285 a month for the bakkie. The contract says R333 270. Both are telling the truth.
clip_script: Every pay-later deal hides its real price, and one sum finds it: add up EVERYTHING you will ever pay. The fridge says R9 499. On hire purchase — R1 424,85 deposit, then R379,90 a month for two and a half years — grab the calculator: total R12 821,85. The fridge costs R3 322,85 extra, and the store owns it until the last payment. Now the bakkie. R3 285 a month sounds doable — that's the design. Hiding in month seventy-two: a balloon payment of R75 250, thirty-five percent of the vehicle, postponed, not forgiven. Deposit plus seventy-two instalments plus balloon: R333 270 for a R215 000 bakkie. R118 270 extra. Pay it, borrow again, or sell the bakkie to settle it — the bubble always bursts. The loan advert plays the same game: R939 a month, but add the service fees and the initiation fee, and R18 000 borrowed costs R7 026 in credit. So the rule that beats every advert: never judge a deal by its monthly number. Total everything, compare it with the price, and make the difference say its name out loud.
visual_style: Price tags peeling back to reveal bigger totals underneath; a calculator stacking deposit, instalments and a swelling red balloon that bursts into a R75 250 bill; a contract's total-cost line highlighted while the advertised instalment shrinks.
mood: Streetwise and protective, the voice of someone who reads the whole contract before the salesperson finishes smiling.
pacing: Quick through the fridge, a suspenseful build to the balloon reveal, a hard stop on R333 270, then calm and firm through the closing rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never let a monthly payment lie to you again.
